title: Describing things
goal: Describe people and things by colour, size and quality, and compare them (bigger, the biggest).
intro:
Good news: Telugu adjectives **never change** for gender or number. *పెద్ద* (pedda, big) stays the same in *పెద్ద ఇల్లు* (big house) and *పెద్ద ఇళ్ళు* (big houses).

To say something *is* big, you either add *-గా ఉంది* ('is in a big way': *పెద్దగా ఉంది*) or turn the adjective into a noun with *-ది* ('a big one': *పెద్దది*). Comparison uses *కంటే* (kaṇṭē, than).

vocab.note: Before a noun: ఎర్ర (erra): ఎర్ర చీర, red sari.
Before a noun: నీలి (nīli) or నీలం రంగు.
From అందం (beauty); -మైన turns nouns into adjectives.

phrases.en: I need one smaller than this.

grammar.title: Adjectives: before the noun, and as predicates
grammar.body:
An adjective goes **before** the noun and **never changes**: *పెద్ద ఇల్లు* (big house), *పెద్ద ఇళ్ళు* (big houses), *పెద్ద అబ్బాయి* (big boy). Colour words have a short form for this position: ఎర్ర, నల్ల, తెల్ల, పచ్చ.

To use an adjective after 'is', Telugu has two patterns:
1. **adj + -గా ఉండు** (-gā uṇḍu) describes how something is or seems: *ఇల్లు పెద్దగా ఉంది* (the house is big).
2. **adj + -ది / -వాడు / -వాళ్ళు** makes 'a ... one' and classifies: *ఈ కారు కొత్తది* (this car is a new one), *అతను మంచివాడు* (he's a good man), *వాళ్ళు మంచివాళ్ళు* (they're good people).

Many adjectives are made from nouns with **-మైన / -ఐన**: అందం (beauty) → అందమైన (beautiful); ఖరీదు (price) → ఖరీదైన (expensive).

examples.en: This car is new (a new one).

grammar.title: Comparing: కంటే (than) and అన్నిటికంటే (most)
grammar.body:
To compare, put **కంటే** (kaṇṭē, than) after the thing you compare with; the adjective stays in its basic form: *X Y కంటే పెద్దది* = X is bigger than Y (lit. X, than Y, big one). There is no separate '-er' form. Pronouns use their oblique form: *నా కంటే* (than me), *దాని కంటే* (than that).

For the superlative, compare with everything: **అన్నిటికంటే** (than all things) or **అందరికంటే** (than everyone).

examples.en: My elder sister is taller than me.
This sari is nicer than that one.
My younger brother is the youngest of all.
This is the best of all.

dialogue.title: The new flat
dialogue.setting: Swathi asks her friend Rekha about the flat she has just moved into.

lines.speaker: Rekha
lines.native: చాలా బాగుంది! పాత ఇంటి కంటే పెద్దది.
lines.roman: chālā bāgundi! pāta iṇṭi kaṇṭē peddadi.
lines.en: Really nice! It's bigger than the old house.

lines.speaker: Rekha
lines.native: మూడు పడకగదులు. వంటగది కూడా పెద్దగా ఉంది.
lines.roman: mūḍu paḍakagadulu. vaṇṭagadi kūḍā peddagā undi.
lines.en: Three bedrooms. The kitchen is big too.

lines.speaker: Rekha
lines.native: హాలు పసుపు రంగు, పడకగదులు నీలం, తెలుపు.
lines.roman: hālu pasupu raṅgu, paḍakagadulu nīlam, telupu.
lines.en: The hall is yellow, the bedrooms blue and white.

lines.speaker: Swathi
lines.en: That must look lovely! Does the house stay cool?

lines.speaker: Rekha
lines.native: అవును, కిటికీలు పెద్దవి. గాలి బాగా వస్తుంది.
lines.roman: avunu, kiṭikīlu peddavi. gāli bāgā vastundi.
lines.en: Yes, the windows are big. There's a good breeze.

lines.speaker: Rekha
lines.en: A bit high, but it's okay.

culture: Colours carry meaning: **yellow** turmeric (*పసుపు*) and red *kumkum* are auspicious and appear at every wedding and festival, while **white** is associated with mourning and widowhood in traditional settings, and **black** is often avoided at celebrations. Comments on someone's weight or complexion (*లావు అయ్యావు!* 'you've put on weight!') are made far more freely than in English-speaking cultures and are usually not meant unkindly.
